glass.$description: near-clear tint. the darkening that keeps white text readable comes from glass.brightness, not from grey (D-010)

kiln.why.why: almost clear white (6 percent) so the scene stays visible; legibility comes from the dimming in glass.brightness and this tint only gives the sheet a surface

solid.$description: D-005 opaque fallback for every glass surface

kiln.why.why: the opaque surface that replaces glass under reduced transparency, forced colours or no backdrop-filter, so content stays readable

quiet.$description: glass-on-glass fill (glass buttons, icon discs). .14 measured 4.25:1 under white text in the mid environment

kiln.why.why: glass on glass for secondary controls, visible as an object and quieter than the one loud solid
the loud solid, white in dark and ink in light, the single strongest mark a pane may carry
top of the placeholder cover gradient, light catching a surface before the real image arrives
bottom of the placeholder cover gradient, so the empty cover still has depth
a faint light at the top of a pane, as on a real sheet of glass lit from above
the sheen fades out lower down, so it reads as light catching the top edge

well.$description: an inset that holds body text inside a glass card (banners). Darkens in dark so secondary text keeps its contrast over lamp-lit photos; the quiet white fill measured 3.57:1 there

kiln.why.why: a slight darkening inside a pane that holds body text, measured to lift banner text from 3.57 to above 4.5 on lamp-lit photos

page.$description: opaque page behind ordinary, non-glass UI (docs, settings, admin). Glass belongs over scenes, not over this

kiln.why.why: the opaque page behind ordinary reading and settings screens, where the scene would only compete with the words

raised.$description: opaque panel on surface.page (sidebars, code headers, callouts)

kiln.why.why: an opaque panel on the page for sidebars, code headers and lists, one step lighter so it reads as on top
an opaque well on the page for code and inputs, one step darker so it reads as recessed

knob.$description: white handle that reads on both themes (slider thumb, switch knob); the ring and shadow separate it from light surfaces

kiln.why.why: a white handle that stays visible on both themes; its ring and shadow separate it from light surfaces
the materials a pane can be made of; each one below states its own role
the floor of a recess or groove, a dimmed patch of the surface in dark and a faint ink tint in light
the far side of the switch bead, a step below white so the bead reads as round
a quiet glass object is lit from above, brighter at its top
a chosen item is a lighter pane of glass resting where it was chosen, so choice reads as a raised object as well as a word
a switch that is on is lit from within, a bright track in dark and a dark one in light
a chosen item standing alone (no track around it) differs from the quiet ones by its glass, brighter in dark and darker in light
a chosen item is a lighter pane of grey glass in dark and white in light
a recessed track, darker than the pane it is cut into

a third step of text for metadata (numbers, code names, counts) on opaque reading surfaces only, the page, the shell and the studio; never on glass, where secondary is already the lowest opacity that passes
text colours flip with the theme because they contrast with a dimmed or lifted scene; secondary keeps the lowest opacity that still measured as passing
words that name a destructive action, a step lighter than the critical mark in dark and darker in light, so they clear 4.5:1 on glass over any scene
the one solid, white in dark and ink in light, lit at its top and shaded at its foot; a promoted action is the same solid glowing with its own light; the system owns no hue (D-024)
hairlines that give panes and controls an edge; the rim is lit from above, brightest along the top edge, faint down the sides and a little stronger at the foot
the edge of a control that has no groove, such as a read-only field, at the opacity that measured 3:1 on glass and pages in both themes
the focus ring is the text colour with a halo of the opposite colour so it shows on any part of any scene

brightness.$description: D-010: backdrop dimming per environment. keeps the scene's colour and detail instead of washing it grey

kiln.why.why: the measured glass recipe in one place, with blur, saturation and the brightness per environment and theme
how high a surface floats, with float for panes, lift for controls and halo for text on thin glass
a field is a well pressed into the glass, so a faint inner shadow at its top edge says it sits below the surface without painting a fill
a solid control is an object on the pane, so it rests with a contact shadow and a soft one below
a press pushes the control back toward the pane, so its shadow tightens
the accent sheet is coloured glass, so the light under it is blue instead of grey
hover lifts the accent closer, so its blue shadow spreads and softens
a press pushes the accent back toward the pane, so its blue shadow tightens
the knob is a bead in a recess, so it casts a short shadow into the well
a recess is made by dimming, shade under the top lip and light on the bottom one, never by an opaque box; the edge measures 3:1 in both themes
the recess keeps its shade when it fills with the one blue, so it still reads as cut into the glass
a field is a groove in the glass, read from its two lips; the lit bottom lip is its 3:1 edge on any surface
the highlighted row is a small lens inside the menu, lit on its top edge like the pane
a label is cut into the surface instead of standing on it, so it never reads as something to press
a portrait carries the pane rim of light and a shade at its foot, so it sits on the glass as a small object
a track is a shallow recess holding its choices, shaded under its top edge by the light from above
the promoted solid glows with its own light, the only glow on a pane
a quiet object rests on the pane on a short soft shadow
a chosen pane rests in its track on a short soft shadow
a lit switch spills a little light onto the pane
a pane that is itself a control, such as a radio card, carries the groove ring as its 3:1 edge, where a level-2 pane alone reads under 1.5:1 in either theme
stroke widths that survive zoom and forced colours, for hairline edges, a 2px ring and a halo wide enough to separate the ring from any backdrop
named gaps from the 4px grid; inset (22px) is the padding inside a pane and is always larger than the gaps between items inside it
a bar the whole hand drags, tall enough to hold its label and value inside it
control heights and icon sizes; 44px is the default so every control is a comfortable touch target, 32px only for dense rows
checkbox, radio and switch knob are 24px marks inside a 44px hit area, large enough to read and to hit
the switch track is 52px wide so the knob travels far enough that on and off read by position as well as colour
the chosen radio shows a 10px dot, a shape that says selected without relying on colour
a slider keeps a usable length and a fixed width, so its pane never resizes while the value changes
a keycap is a caption-sized slab, big enough to read the key printed on it inside a sentence
a floating action button is 56px, larger than any other control on the screen
a popup list stops at about seven rows and scrolls inside itself, so the page under it stays visible
the typing space in a field full of chips keeps room for a short word, so the reader can always add one
a radio card keeps room for its title and a line of detail before the row wraps
a rating star is big enough to count at a glance, inside a 44px press area
a top bar holds 44px targets with room above and below, never cramped against the edge
a bottom-nav destination stacks its icon and label in a target taller than 44px
a destination is at least 64px wide, easy to hit with a thumb
a navigation panel is a column of links, each with a line of description
a segment is never narrower than a short word, so modes do not crowd
a navigation column is 280px, wide enough for labels on one line beside the content
panel, inner and media corners nest by the padding between them, and round is for things that are held
drawings in diagrams are marks on a plan, so they get a small corner that keeps narrow plates from turning into pills and hiding their width
a checkbox is a held control with soft corners, yet stays square enough to read differently from a round radio

reading.$description: paragraphs people read for more than a line or two

kiln.why.why: type roles mapped to the scale, so components ask for a role (label, body, title) and never a pixel size
motion roles mapped to durations and distances, so hover, press and entry always feel the same across components
a spinner turns once a second or so, steady enough to read as working and never frantic; zero under reduced motion
a skeleton fades in and out slowly, so waiting reads as calm rather than as a flashing alert; zero under reduced motion
status fills each with the text colour computed to pass on it; every use also says the status in words
the info tone as a small glyph colour only, so the scene keeps its hue while the glyph shape and spoken word carry the meaning too
the positive tone as a small glyph colour only, so the scene keeps its hue while the glyph shape and spoken word carry the meaning too
the warning tone as a small glyph colour only, so the scene keeps its hue while the glyph shape and spoken word carry the meaning too
the critical tone as a small glyph colour only, so the scene keeps its hue while the glyph shape and spoken word carry the meaning too
grid columns, gutters, margins and container widths per breakpoint, so pages share one rhythm
stacking roles mapped to the z order, so overlays and sticky bars always sit above content
breakpoints by role, used only for layout changes, never to hide content
a neutral backdrop for diagrams and layout demos, where no scene is shown, with a faint gradient for the glass to blur and fine construction lines that show the grid the panes sit on

diagram columns in the loud solid, white in dark and ink in light, so they stand well off the ground in both themes, read as the place where content goes, and carry column numbers in the opposite tone at 4.5:1 or more; the system spends no hue on diagrams (D-024)
margins are hatched in the text colour so they are told apart from columns by pattern as well as by tone
the default backdrop for showing a component: a near-black sweep (a pale one in light) with one soft light from the top left, so the glass has a gradient to blur and the component stays the subject
a disabled control fades to half, and its reason is written beside it because a faded control cannot be focused to ask
the faint point of a breath or a fade-in, still visible as a recess on bright scenes

the stack of glass: level 1 a pane, 2 a surface inside it, 3 an overlay, 4 a popover, each a measured step from its neighbours, and a scrim that halves the scene under an overlay; the streak is light catching the curve of the top edge
each level floats a step higher on a longer shadow; every slab has an edge all round; the loud solid blooms; a track is a well
in dark, a few white parts give off light instead of reflecting it: what is on, what is now, and the one promoted action. Everything else reflects. In light nothing glows.
the promoted action shines with its own light, the strongest glow on a pane and the only strong one
a lit value or a powered part (a slider's filled channel, a switch that is on) gives off a soft light
a small mark that says now (the current step, where a value stops) glows a little wider than its size
a mesh gradient is a scene or a piece of media, never a control's fill: the world supplies the hue and the glass shows it (P1)
the pale ground the pools sit in, light enough that glass over it reads as dimmed, not dirty
the warm pool at the top left, where light seems to come from, matching the one light from above
the coral pool at the top right that carries the warmth across the top of the scene
the deepest pool, low in the frame, so the mesh has a dark point and the glass a bright one to test
the lilac pool at the bottom left that joins the violet back to the pale ground
a warm preset for products whose world is firelight, food or evening: amber and rose over a plum low point
the ember preset's ground, placed where the ember light falls
the ember preset's pool a, placed where the ember light falls
the ember preset's pool b, placed where the ember light falls
the ember preset's pool c, placed where the ember light falls
the ember preset's pool d, placed where the ember light falls
a cool preset for products whose world is water, air or health: aqua and sky over an indigo low point
the tide preset's ground, placed where the tide light falls
the tide preset's pool a, placed where the tide light falls
the tide preset's pool b, placed where the tide light falls
the tide preset's pool c, placed where the tide light falls
the tide preset's pool d, placed where the tide light falls
an evening preset for media and night scenes: lilac and rose over a deep navy low point
the dusk preset's ground, placed where the dusk light falls
the dusk preset's pool a, placed where the dusk light falls
the dusk preset's pool b, placed where the dusk light falls
the dusk preset's pool c, placed where the dusk light falls
the dusk preset's pool d, placed where the dusk light falls
the pools of a mesh are blurred until they flow, which is what makes it a mesh and not a set of radial gradients
a mesh object's ambient light is strong enough to tint the pane under it and faint enough that it never reads as a second object
named proportions, so media keeps its shape at any width and nothing jumps when it loads
one to one, for avatars, app icons and grid tiles
four to three, the shape of most camera photos
sixteen to nine, the shape of video and wide covers
three to four, for people and posters held upright
twenty-one to nine, for banners and cinematic headers
a dialog is one measure wide, so its question and answer read as one short block
a wide dialog or a bottom sheet on a tablet, room for a short form
a drawer is about the width of a phone, so navigation inside it reads the same everywhere
a popover holds a sentence and a couple of controls, never a page
a tooltip wraps after a few words so it never grows into a paragraph
the toast column is narrow enough to leave the content beside it readable
a bottom sheet stops short of the top so the screen it came from still shows above it
the grabber is wide enough to find with a thumb, with a 44px press area around it
the categorical order for charts, dark steps by default and light steps in the light theme, both validated against the glass surfaces
an ordered magnitude such as confidence is one hue stepping from faint to strong, never categorical hues (D-032)
an ordered magnitude such as confidence is one hue stepping from faint to strong, never categorical hues (D-032)
